text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon: Prime minister's parleys a waste of time.
- Russia said ready to downgrade cooperation with Iran.
- Government: Russian gas prospects don't preclude regional options.
- Israel, European Union to resume poultry imports.
- U.S. businessman Jeffrey Keil not worried by Bank Hapoalim tender delay.
GLOBES
- Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman backs tax reform -- but gives preference to budget cut.
HAARETZ
- Egypt's Foreign Minister Amr Moussa tells Haaretz: Egyptian mediation effort ineffective. Continuous rejectionism of Israeli government doesn't clear way out of crisis.
- Tax reform being drafted.
MAARIV

- Lawmakers from the coalition are conducting secret negotiations with the Palestinians. Groups led by Gideon Ezra of Likud and Hani al-Hassan are conducting "academic discussions on final status". Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office: "The prime minister is updated on the contacts and he has no opposition. It's not official negotiations."
- Hizbollah guerrillas in Lebanon threaten to carry out suicide attacks because of the "pig poster".

- Gallup poll of 500 Israeli Jews shows 68 percent of Israelis unhappy with the the prime minister's performance in the last political crisis, 23 percent are happy and 9 percent don't know. Poll has 4.5 percent margin of error.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Ariel Sharon accuses Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai of being too close to the Americans. Background is Mordechai's support for Israel's signing the treaty to wipe out chemical weapons.
- Writers and intellectuals appeal to Netanyahu to moderate the incitement.
